body:
> Range derived nodes _min_value_ property triggers the signal _value_changed_ when changed.
> 
> As I expected, the _max_value_ property doesn't trigger the value_changed signal when it changes but the _value_ property does.

What triggers the `value_changed` signal emission is the `value` actually being changed. Changing either `min_value`/`max_value` might result in the old `value` being outside of the new range/limits, and this is what causes the `value` to be changed / forced into such new range. So yes, depending on the setup changing `min_value`/`max_value` can trigger changing `value` (and hence `value_changed` signal).

Some examples:
```gdscript
extends Range

func _ready() -> void:
	print_values()
	case1() # <--------------- CHANGE
	print_values()

func _on_value_changed(new_value: float) -> void:
	print("value_changed(%s)" % [new_value])

func print_values() -> void:
	print("value: {value} min_value: {min_value} max_value: {max_value} allow_lesser: {allow_lesser} allow_greater: {allow_greater}".format(self))


func case1() -> void:
	print("min_value = 25.0")
	min_value = 25.0
	
func case2() -> void:
	print("allow_lesser = true")
	allow_lesser = true
	print_values()
	print("min_value = 25.0")
	min_value = 25.0
	
func case3() -> void:
	print("min_value = -25.0")
	min_value = -25.0
	
func case4() -> void:
	print("min_value = -25.0")
	min_value = -25.0
	print_values()
	print("max_value = -10.0")
	max_value = -10.0
	
func case5() -> void:
	print("allow_greater = true")
	allow_greater = true
	print_values()
	print("min_value = -25.0")
	min_value = -25.0
	print_values()
	print("max_value = -10.0")
	max_value = -10.0
```
Outputs (v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]):
```
# case1()
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
min_value = 25.0
value_changed(25.0)
value: 25.0 min_value: 25.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false

# case2()
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
allow_lesser = true
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: true allow_greater: false
min_value = 25.0
value: 0.0 min_value: 25.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: true allow_greater: false

# case3()
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
min_value = -25.0
value: 0.0 min_value: -25.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false

# case4()
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
min_value = -25.0
value: 0.0 min_value: -25.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
max_value = -10.0
value_changed(-10.0)
value: -10.0 min_value: -25.0 max_value: -10.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false

# case5()
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: false
allow_greater = true
value: 0.0 min_value: 0.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: true
min_value = -25.0
value: 0.0 min_value: -25.0 max_value: 100.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: true
max_value = -10.0
value: 0.0 min_value: -25.0 max_value: -10.0 allow_lesser: false allow_greater: true
```

So I don't see a bug in here.


---


Also note there's [`Object.set_block_signals`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/classes/class_object.html#class-object-method-set-block-signals) method which could be used to force not emitting signals in some scope, but I'm not sure if doing something like below won't break some internal logic for `Range`. So use with caution.
```gdscript
(...)
set_block_signals(true)
min_value = ...
set_block_signals(false)
(...)
```
Thanks for the explanation, not a bug then! 🙂

Setting `min_value` on a `SpinBox` can trigger the signal, though (in Godot 4.4.1_stable). If you set `step` to `10` and change `min_value` to something that isn't a multiple of `10`, it will change the `value` and trigger the signal.

For example, suppose the `value` is `50` and the `min_value` is `10`. If you change `min_value` to `5` or `15`, it will add `5` to the `value` and trigger the `value_changed` signal. If you change it to `12` it will add `2` to the `value`. 

(You can easily test this by changing a `SpinBox`'s settings in the inspector as the game is running. I haven't tested this on other Range types.)

The tooltip says `value` will always be rounded to a multiple of `step`, but it doesn't say anything about being offset by `min_value`.

---

I had this problem while trying to re-use the same spinbox for two related things, depending on which one was active, but they have different min and max values, so I had to change them at runtime. But since there's no way to set min without triggering the signal, I had to use two different spinboxes. Not a big deal, though, it's just the context of how I noticed this.
